messages.content: I'll execute this task now. Since no specific topic was supplied with the instruction, I'll demonstrate the requested workflow — decomposing into sub-questions, retrieving the relevant Wikipedia article sections, and noting the sources cited in each — on a representative, heavily-cited flagship article: **"Artificial intelligence"** (a Wikipedia-level featured article whose sections are densely referenced). I'll dispatch parallel research agents for each sub-question.

subtopics: Wikipedia article 'Artificial intelligence' — History section: retrieve/summarize the key events and claims in that section (founding 1956 Dartmouth workshop, AI winters, booms), and list the specific sources/references cited in that section (author, work, year where visible in citations).

Wikipedia article 'Artificial intelligence' — Goals and Capabilities sections (reasoning, problem-solving, knowledge representation, planning/decision-making, learning, natural language processing, perception, robotics): summarize the content and list the specific sources cited in those sections.

Wikipedia article 'Artificial intelligence' — Techniques/Approaches sections (symbolic AI, search and optimization, logic, probabilistic methods, machine learning, deep learning/neural networks, and subfields like computer vision/NLP/robotics): summarize and list the specific sources cited.

Wikipedia article 'Artificial intelligence' — Applications section (healthcare, finance, transportation, generative AI, military, etc.): summarize the content and list the specific sources cited in that section.

Wikipedia article 'Artificial intelligence' — Ethics, Risks, and Regulation sections (bias, existential risk, transparency, EU AI Act, governance): summarize the content and list the specific sources cited in those sections.
